html:
The ancient people of the Carpathian lands and the lower Danube, in what is now Romania and Moldova, related to the Thracians. The map shows them in 100 BCE on both banks of the lower Danube.

Greek writers called those near the Black Sea the Getae and Romans called the people Daci; they were probably one people with one language. They farmed, mined gold and salt, and built hill forts with walls of cut stone. Their god Zalmoxis promised a life after death.

Around 82 BCE the king Burebista united the tribes and built a large but short-lived kingdom, from the Black Sea coast to the middle Danube. He beat the Celtic Boii and worried Rome, but was killed in 44 BCE, the same year as Julius Caesar. The kingdom split, then united again under Decebalus; its later shape is Dacia. Their religious and royal centre was Sarmizegetusa Regia in the mountains. To the south lay Thrace and to the east the Sarmatians.
sum: The ancient people of the Carpathian lands and the lower Danube, in what is now Romania and Moldova, related to the Thracians. The map shows them in 100 BCE on both banks of the lower Danube.
